title: A Lagrangian approach for prescribed mass solutions of cubic-quintic Schrödinger equations and $L^2$-supercritical problems
summary: We study the existence of radially symmetric solutions of the following nonlinear scalar field equations in $\mathbb R^N$ ($N \geq 2$): $$ (*)_m \quad - Δu + μu = g(u) \quad \text{in}\ {\mathbb R}^N, \quad {1\over 2} \int_{{\mathbb R}^N} u^2\, dx = m,$$ where $g(s) \in C({\mathbb R},{\mathbb R})$, $m > 0$ and $μ\in {\mathbb R}$ is an unknown Lagrangian multiplier. We take an approach using a Lagrangian formulation of $(*)_m$: $$J_m(μ,u)={1\over 2}\int_{{\mathbb R}^N} |\nabla u|^2\,dx -\int_{{\mathbb R}^N} G(u)\,dx +μ\left({1\over 2}\int_{{\mathbb R}^N} u^2\, dx-m\right) \in…
